data.description:
# Intake Brief: Audit freshness invalidates only on this work item's own data change

## Problem statement

The audit freshness gate (`_check_audit_freshness` / `_compute_content_fingerprint`
in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`) invalidates a stored audit when any
fingerprint component changes. The original formulation fingerprinted
**whole-repo** state (git HEAD sha + work-item description hash + Key Files +
whole-repo working-tree hash), so any commit or uncommitted/untracked change
anywhere in the repository — even one from an *unrelated* work item — invalidated
every stored audit and re-triggered the full audit pipeline.

**Observed failure (SA-0MSN04X2S006ONH0):** audited "Ready to close: Yes" at HEAD
`310773d5`; afterwards an unrelated work item (SA-0MSQ026T3009QY2L) merged
`aaabdede` to dev, the fingerprint changed (`58947e06…` matched recomputation at
`310773d5` but not at `aaabdede`), the re-audit ran and blocked on the pre-flight
full-suite cache gate — a verified item stuck in review.

**Current state (2026-10-21, HEAD `fe85415a3`):** the whole-repo components have
**already been replaced** by per-touched-file scoping (SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P, done):
the payload is now `{path_states, description_hash, key_files}` where each
touched path contributes its committed state (blob hash at HEAD, else the latest
touching commit) plus its narrowed working-tree state. An unrelated commit or
working-tree change now invalidates **only if it touches a file in the item's
touched set** (commits referencing the item id + comment-recorded commit hashes +
Key Files). The whole-repo HEAD sha is no longer a component, and
`_resolve_working_tree_hash` no longer exists. The observed failure case is
therefore **no longer reproducible** with today's formula.

The remaining delta of this item is the **strict rule** recorded in the original
Q&A: "An audit is only invalidated if there is a change to this work item's data
AFTER the audit was created." That rule is stronger than the current
per-touched-file formula — it requires a fingerprint over the item's own data
only (title + description, which contains the ACs and Key Files), with **zero git
calls**, so even a committed/uncommitted change to a file this item touched does
not invalidate.

## Users

- Audit operators / automated dispatchers relying on `audit_runner.py` freshness
  short-circuit (SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT) to skip re-audits of unchanged items.

**User story:** "As an audit operator, I want a stored audit to remain valid
unless THIS work item's own data changes, so unrelated repository activity
(including changes to files this item happened to touch) doesn't invalidate my
audits."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_compute_content_fingerprint` is computed from the **work item's own data
   only** — the item's title + description (the description contains the ACs and
   the Key Files section, so `key_files` may remain in the payload as a
   deterministic derivative of it). The per-path git components (committed HEAD
   blob hashes, working-tree state) and the whole-repo HEAD component are

## Goal

Prevent the audit runner's Phase-1 code-quality scan from passing non-Python files (YAML, JSON, Markdown, etc.) to ruff as explicit file arguments, eliminating false-positive `invalid-syntax` findings that get auto-created as work items.

## Background / Root cause

On 2026-08-11, an implement self-review audit ran `run_code_quality(files=cq_scope_files)` with the git changed-file list, which included `proxy/config-cheap.yaml` (uncommitted changes at the time). `_run_ruff_check` invoked `ruff check <yaml-file>` — ruff parses YAML as Python and emitted 121 false-positive `invalid-syntax` findings, which `create_epics_for_findings` auto-created as work items under the Quality Improvement epic (LP-0MSJFTRUW0076Z5Y). Those stale items were later marked completed/in_review and drained one-by-one by the herdr downtime audit tier (~59 dispatches in one evening).

The `.ruff.toml` `exclude = ["*.yaml", "*.yml"]` fix (commit 7580063) is **insufficient**: ruff only honors `exclude` for directory scans; explicit file arguments bypass it (verified: `ruff check config-cheap.yaml` with the exclude in place still returns invalid-syntax findings, while `ruff check .` returns `[]`).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `run_ruff` / `_run_ruff_check` filter the `files` list to Python extensions (`.py`, `.pyi`, `.ipynb`) before invoking ruff; non-Python files are skipped and never passed as explicit paths.
2. A regression test asserts ruff is never invoked with a `.yaml`/`.yml` file path when the changed-file list includes one, and that no finding work items are created for non-Python files.
3. Directory-scan behavior (`files=None`) is unchanged.
4. Genuine ruff findings on `.py` files are unaffected (existing tests pass).

## Summary

The audit runner's code-quality scan is documented to lint only the work item's changed files (`SA-0MSKB6VWU000RT58` AC1: "the code-quality scan runs only over the git changed-file list … not the full repo"), but it silently falls back to a **whole-repo** scan whenever the changed-file list is empty. For an item whose work is already committed to `dev` (the normal post-merge state, and the state the merge gate integrates to), `git diff --name-only HEAD` + `git status --porcelain` are both empty, so `run_code_quality(files=cq_scope_files or None)` receives `None` and lints the entire repository. Any pre-existing critical/high ruff finding in an unrelated file then blocks Phase 1 of every audit in that repo — a recurrence of the defect class fixed by `SA-0MSG83Z4Z004YH2P` ("EXE001 misclassified as 'high' severity blocks audits on unrelated files") and a contradiction of `SA-0MSKB6VWU000RT58` AC1.

## Repro

1. Work item `LP-0MTYAZFGN003BYQS` (llm) is merged to `origin/dev`; the local checkout is clean at the delivered commit `66ddbe93`.
2. `git diff --name-only HEAD` and `git status --porcelain` are both empty.
3. Run `audit_runner.py issue LP-0MTYAZFGN003BYQS --force`: `_git_changed_files` returns `[]`, so `run_code_quality(files=None)` scans the whole repo.
4. The whole-repo scan returns 4 findings, all outside the item's change set:
   - `ruff F841` (critical) `proxy/tests/test_watchdog_upstream_cancellation.py:197,277`
   - `ruff I001` (medium) `proxy/tests/test_compaction_summarizer.py:594`, `proxy/tests/test_startup_ramp.py:503`
5. Phase 1 blocks on the critical findings; every AC is demoted `met → partial` and Phase 2 is skipped; `Ready to close: No`.

Verified directly: `run_code_quality(project_root=<llm>, files=[the item's 4 changed files])` returns **0 findings** — the item's own work is lint-clean.

## Impact (observed)

- The audit of `LP-0MTYAZFGN003BYQS` (2026-09-26) produced a spurious `Ready to close: No` from findings belonging to other work items. The item was only accepted because the Phase 1 false-positive screen *also* degraded (provider error / concurrency limit), leaving the run fallback-tainted and the lifecycle restored to `completed`/`in_review`.
- Had the screen succeeded, the `F841` findings would have been classified `genuine` and the unrelated item would have been **demoted** `in_review → open`.
- The findings already have tracking items (quality epics): `LP-0MUHSWSI8004AFU4`, `LP-0MUHSWS8M001QY46`, `LP-0MUHVMLGB0056C0K`.

## Suggested fix

- When the git changed-file list is empty, scope the code-quality scan to the item's **Key Files** and/or its committed diff (the commits the merge gate resolved, e.g. `git diff-tree -r --name-only <commit>^..<commit>`), instead of falling back to the whole repo.
- An empty effective scope should lint nothing (skip with a documented reason), never the entire repository.
- Cover the already-merged / clean-checkout case in `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py`.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_git_changed_files`, `_resolve_touched_files`, and both `run_code_quality(files=cq_scope_files or None)` call sites (Phase 1 scan ~L11011, remediation re-scan ~L10818)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_phase1.py` — Phase 1 code-quality scan call-argument tests (scope resolution)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_remediation.py` — remediation re-scan tests (second call site)
- `skill/code_review/scripts/linter_runner.py` — `_run_ruff_check` treats a falsy `files` list as a whole-project scan, so an empty scope must skip the call rather than pass `[]`
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — the code-quality scoping contract this bug contradicts

## Acceptance Criteria

1. For an item whose work is already committed and whose checkout is clean, the audit code-quality scan lints only the item's files (Key Files and/or its delivered commits), never the whole repo.
2. An empty effective scope lints nothing: the scan is skipped with a documented reason surfaced through the existing `cq_skipped_reason` (rendered as `code_quality_skipped_reason`), rather than scanning the whole repository. Passing `files=[]` is not sufficient — `_run_ruff_check` treats a falsy list as a whole-project scan.

- **Recurrence prevention:** add `pi@local` to `syncAllowedAuthors` in `.worklog/config.yaml` for this project (operator-chosen option c), so pi-session-authored sync commits pass the gate. # Audit wall-clock reduction: diagnose and fix why audits take hours

## Problem statement

Item-level audits routinely take hours (measured: 4.25h for a 10-child parent) and
even single-item audits exceed 30 minutes, to the point where operators avoid
running them and release gates stall. Instrumented data from every audit log on
this host shows the cost is not one slow operation but a **long chain of slow,
serial LLM calls against a 2-slot local proxy, oversubscribed by a concurrency
ceiling of 6**, with roughly **18% of total call time producing no usable result**
(timeouts and JSON re-asks).

## Users

- **Release producer** — blocked at the `ship` audit gate, waiting hours for a re-audit.
- **Implementation agent** — cannot complete the implement skill's self-review audit within a session budget.
- **Operator** — avoids auditing, so `in_review` items accumulate unreviewed.

Example user stories:

- As a release producer, I want a single-item audit to finish in **≤ 10 minutes** on a healthy proxy so the `dev`→`main` gate is not a multi-hour stall.
- As an implementation agent, I want a parent audit with 10 children to finish in **≤ 30 minutes** so it fits one session and aborts less often.
- As an operator, I want a **reproducible measurement** of audit wall-clock so I can verify a change actually helped instead of guessing.

## Diagnosis — why audits are slow (measured)

Source: `Per-call timing:` lines from `~/.audit_debug/*/*.log`
(465 logs, 491 distinct work items, **1,637 instrumented LLM calls, 140.8h total**).
Reproduce with the script specified in AC1.

### Call-time distribution by phase

| Context | calls | total | p50 | p90 | max |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `parent` (Phase 1 parent screen) | 450 | **48.3h** | 220s | 954s | 2,705s |
| `child` (Phase 1 child screen) | 412 | **38.1h** | 227s | 633s | 1,572s |
| `verdict_reask` (JSON-contract retry) | 121 | **18.7h** | 461s | 1,466s | 2,372s |
| `phase2_deep` | 285 | 16.0h | 102s | 513s | 1,800s |
| `phase2_child` | 316 | 15.8h | 101s | 529s | 1,775s |
| `false-positive-screen` | 53 | 3.9h | 168s | 600s | 1,200s |

Median call **158s**; 76% of calls ≥ 60s; 35% ≥ 300s.

### Root causes, ranked by measured cost

1. **Phase 1 screening is 62% of all call time (86.4h).** It runs as parent
   screen → N child screens, each a fresh full-prompt session, and averages
   220–227s per call for what is structurally *screening*, not deep analysis.
2. **Concurrency ceiling (6) is 3× the proxy's real capacity (2 slots).**
   `GET /llama/local/status` reports `total_slots: 2`, `available_slots: 0`.
   Six concurrent `pi` sessions queue behind two slots; the queue wait is
   charged against each call's own timeout budget, inflating p90 latency.
3. **~25h of pure timeout waste.** Calls landing exactly on a budget:
   **96 at 600s** (child-screen budget), **13 at 1,800s**, **86 at 90s**.
   Each returns a `partial` fallback that does no work and forces a later re-run.
4. **18.7h of JSON-contract re-asks.** 121 `verdict_reask` calls exist only
   because the first response was not parseable JSON — and the re-ask itself
   has p50 461s, *slower* than the call it retries.
5. **No reuse across the pipeline.** Every phase re-sends its own large prompt;
   a single edited description or touched file invalidates the content
   fingerprint and discards all prior screening work.

### Where the levers are

| Lever | Measured/expected saving | Status in code |
|---|---|---|
| Size concurrency to real slot capacity | removes queue-induced inflation + most 600s/1,800s timeout waste | ceiling hardcoded default 6 (`process_semaphore.py`); slot-status query exists but only used for *child* ceiling |
| Eliminate JSON re-asks | up to 18.7h of 140.8h | `_reask_json_array_once` exists as the fallback; parse robustness not hardened |
| Batch Phase 1 parent+children into one call | collapses N+1 screens to ~1 | `--batch-phase2` exists for Phase 2 only, off by default |
| Route Phase 1 to a fast model | Phase 1 is 62% of time, low-reasoning work | `phase1_model` plumbing exists but **no CLI/env surface**; tiered-model item was demoted |
| Adaptive timeout + degrade early | converts 25h of dead time into fast partials | fixed 600s/1,800s budgets |

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Reproducible measurement harness committed.** A script (e.g. `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py`) parses `Per-call timing:` lines from `~/.audit_debug/` and prints the per-context table above (calls, total, p50, p90, max, and count-at-budget). Running it on this host reproduces the baseline numbers in this brief within expected variance, and it is covered by a unit test with a fixture corpus.
- **Baseline is recorded and a target is set.** The measured baseline (1,637 calls / 140.8h / 62% Phase 1 / 18% wasted) is committed to `docs/dev/` and a small-item audit wall-clock target of **≤ 10 minutes** (healthy proxy, no concurrent audits) is stated and used as the regression gate.
- **Concurrency ceiling is sized to real capacity.** The audit runner derives its parallel-call ceiling from the live slot status (`available_slots` / `total_slots`) with a safe floor, never exceeding that capacity, and falls back to the static ceiling when the query fails. Unit tests prove: 2-slot proxy ⇒ ceiling ≤ 2; failed query ⇒ configured fallback; explicit `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` remains authoritative.
- **JSON-contract re-asks are substantially eliminated.** Parse robustness is hardened (strict schema instruction, tolerant extraction, single retry only on genuine failures) and a regression test proves a well-formed model response is never re-asked. Measured `verdict_reask` count drops to ≤ 2% of calls in a re-measurement on the same corpus.
- **Phase 1 call count is reduced.** Parent + child Phase 1 screening is batched and/or routed to a faster model so a 10-child parent issues materially fewer serial Phase 1 calls; a test proves the call count for a 10-child parent is reduced versus the current N+1 structure, with no change to `met`/`unmet`/`partial`/`adjusted` verdict semantics or the ready-to-close gate.
- **Post-change measurement demonstrates the reduction.** Re-running the AC1 harness after implementation shows overall audit LLM wall-clock reduced by **≥ 50%** on a representative audit, with no increase in `partial`-fallback rate and no relaxation of any closure criterion.
- **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, the audit skill reference, and `docs/dev/audit-phase2-measured-report.md` (or a superseding report).
- **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Verdict semantics are frozen:** no change may relax the ready-to-close gate;
  a `partial` fallback must never degrade to `met`. Correctness outranks speed.
- **Do not simply raise timeouts.** The historical 900→1200→1800s bumps masked
  the inefficiency; this work reduces actual work, not the ceiling.
- Only **2 local proxy slots** exist — any parallel design must be safe below
  saturation, and must not starve interactive `pi` sessions.
- The runner is a `[READ-ONLY AUDIT]` except the already-documented persistence,
  lifecycle, and ruff-remediation exceptions — no new state mutations.
- Changes land on `dev` only; full suite must be green at the push gate.

## Existing state

- Prior epics `SA-0MSADWWH3003N82D` (Phase 2 perf, P1–P6) and P7
  (`SA-0MSF3RXU8005CFGD`) are **complete** and moved the bottleneck from Phase 2
  to Phase 1; that is now confirmed by measurement (§Diagnosis).
- Existing reports: `docs/dev/audit-phase2-performance-evaluation.md`,
  `docs/dev/audit-phase1-performance-evaluation.md`,
  `docs/dev/audit-phase2-measured-report.md`.
- Existing levers already in code but not effective by default: `--batch-phase2`,
  `phase1_model` plumbing, child-verdict reuse, content fingerprint gate,
  per-phase checkpoints.
- Related open items: `SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0` (simplify audit freshness) and
  `SA-0MUSZJRB9006ZCHE` (queue/concurrency tuning, done but ceiling remains 6).

## Desired change

A measurable, repeatable audit performance programme: (1) lock in the harness and
baseline, (2) size concurrency to real slot capacity, (3) eliminate JSON re-asks,
(4) collapse Phase 1 call count via batching and/or a fast Phase 1 model, and
(5) re-measure to prove ≥ 50% wall-clock reduction — decomposed into child work
items during the plan stage.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Phase 1 screening, `_call_pi`, timeout
  and parallelism resolution, `_reask_json_array_once`, batch-mode gates.
- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — concurrency ceiling default (6).
- `skill/audit/scripts/scan.py` — slot-status query reused for the ceiling.
- `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py` — new measurement harness (AC1).
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_concurrency.py` — ceiling-from-slots tests.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_json_contract_reask.py` — re-ask elimination tests.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_phase1.py` — Phase 1 call-count tests.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`,
  `docs/dev/audit-phase2-measured-report.md` — documentation.

## Related work

- `SA-0MSK9IOEF007PP5S` — **Audit skill: reduce audit wall-clock time (audits far too slow)** (completed). This is the closest prior attempt and shares the same problem statement. It delivered the content freshness gate, gated child cascade, and scoped code-quality scan — **partial overlap**. This item is deliberately scoped to the *residual* drivers those levers did not remove (Phase 1 = 62% of call time, concurrency ceiling 6 vs 2 real slots, JSON re-asks, ~25h of timeout waste), plus the measurement harness needed to prove any future change is real. It does not re-do the freshness/cascade/scoping work.
- `SA-0MSADWWH3003N82D` — Audit skill Phase 2 performance evaluation and improvement (complete).
- `SA-0MSF3RXU8005CFGD` — Phase 1 performance treatment (P7) (complete).
- `SA-0MUSZJRB9006ZCHE` — audit queue timeout / concurrency ceiling tuning (complete; ceiling still 6).
- `SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0` — simplify audit freshness invalidation (open).
- `SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL` — audit reliability RCA (reliability, not latency).
- Docs: `docs/dev/audit-phase1-performance-evaluation.md`,
  `docs/dev/audit-phase2-performance-evaluation.md`,
  `docs/dev/audit-phase2-measured-report.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched `audit`, `speed up`, `Phase 2`, and all prior Phase 1/2 performance items.
One partial overlap found (`SA-0MSK9IOEF007PP5S`, completed) — its delivered ACs
(freshness gate, child-cascade opt-in, scoped code-quality scan) are **not** the
same as this item's ACs, and re-measurement shows the problem persists. Scope
rewritten to the residual gaps only; recorded above under Related work. One
accidental duplicate created during this intake (`SA-0MVF1GHVX008Q66T`) was
closed as a duplicate of this item.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the logged `Per-call timing` corpus is representative; it is
  derived from this host's real audit history (491 items) and is the only
  latency evidence available.
- **Risk (quality):** batching Phase 1 into fewer, larger calls could reduce
  verdict quality — mitigated by keeping per-AC verdict semantics and comparing
  verdict output before/after on a fixed item set.
- **Risk (contention):** a parallel design sized to slots could still contend
  with interactive sessions — mitigated by a floor of 1 and never exceeding
  `available_slots`.
- **Risk (scope creep):** adjacency to freshness simplification
  (`SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0`) and the merge-gate work — those stay separate items;
  this epic links rather than absorbs them.
- **Risk (measurement):** historical numbers were taken under concurrent audit
  load; targets must be re-measured clean-room for a fair comparison.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Is the complaint about *all* audits or a specific class (single-item vs
  multi-child parent)?
  **Answer (operator, seed prompt):** "Audits take far too long" — general.
  Diagnosis shows both are affected: single-item ~10–30 min, 10-child parent
  4.25h. Scope therefore covers both, with the parent case as the primary target.
  Source: seed prompt `/intake` request; evidence: per-context table above.

- **Q:** Should the fix raise timeouts or reduce actual work?
  **Answer (derived from prior art):** Reduce actual work. Prior bumps
  (900→1200→1800s) are documented as masking inefficiency
  (`docs/dev/audit-phase2-performance-evaluation.md` §1). Source: repo docs.

- **Q:** Is switching off the local proxy (to a remote model) acceptable?
  **Answer (OPEN QUESTION — producer decision):** assumed *permitted but not
  required*; the plan prefers fast/local routing and treats remote routing
  (e.g. `deepseek-v4-flash`) as an option to confirm. Source: this intake;
  needs producer confirmation at plan review.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-21T15:12:22Z — plan skill decomposed this epic into 7 children (1 pre-existing task + 6 new
  features) and wired 11 dependency edges in test-first ordering (harness/baseline →
  concurrency ceiling + JSON re-asks + child-screen budget → Phase 1 call count →
  post-change verification → documentation). Parent AC markers were normalised from
  `1.` numbering to `- ` bullets and unwrapped to single lines so the shared
  tree-coverage review can machine-check parent→child AC coverage; each child carries
  a "Parent ACn traceability" bullet. Coverage review: 100% (action `proceed`).

# implement.py drive reports child as failed on session timeout even when child completed (no terminal-state reconciliation)

## Problem statement

`implement.py drive` treats a per-child session timeout (`subprocess.TimeoutExpired` in `_default_session_spawner`) as a hard child failure — it stops the whole epic chain and reports `success: false` / `failed_child` — without reconciling against the child's actual work-item state. Observed in the WL-0MVGEB3IP002V8IB epic (three children): each child session was killed at the per-child timeout (3600s/7200s/10800s) after the child had already committed and pushed to `dev`, yet `drive` reported:

```
"result": "failed",
"reason": "Child session for WL-0MVGU4S58003IRXV timed out after 3600s."
```

In two of the three cases the child had verifiably reached terminal state (status `completed`/stage `in_review` + commit on `origin/dev`); in the third the work was pushed but the final `StatusLifecycle` terminal update had not yet run, leaving the item stranded `in-progress` (manually finalised afterwards).

## Users

- **herdr downtime dispatcher / producers** driving epics: needs `drive` to complete children reliably and report truthful per-child results.
- **Epic owner / auditor** reading `drive --json` output: a `failed` child that is actually `completed`/`in_review` on `dev` is a false negative; the audit trail is wrong.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Timeout-reconciliation pass succeeds when child is terminal.** When a driven child's session times out but the child's work item has reached a terminal state (status `completed`/`done` or stage `in_review`) with its commit pushed to `dev`, the drive report does **not** fail that child and does **not** stop the chain: it records the actual terminal status (result `ok`/`completed-late` with the terminal evidence), continues driving remaining children, and advances the parent when all children are terminal. Unit-testable with a fake spawner that simulates a timeout while `wl show` reports the child as terminal.
2. **Non-terminal children still fail hard.** When a driven child's session times out and the child is **not** terminal, the existing hard-failure behaviour is preserved (report fails the child, stops the chain) — regression-guarded.
3. **Stranded in-progress children are detected and finalised.** A child whose work was pushed to `dev` but whose item is still `in-progress` after its session is killed (missing terminal update) is detected at the next `phase_parent`/`drive` pass and finalised to `completed`/`in_review` (or a clear diagnostic is emitted naming the stranded item) — the item must not remain an orphaned `in-progress` blocking `wl next`.
4. **Drive report distinguishes timeout outcomes.** The per-child `children_driven` entry or failure reason distinguishes "timed out but child completed" from "timed out, child incomplete" with the terminal evidence (status/stage/commit) so the report is truthful.
5. **Tests pass.** Existing tests for `phase_drive`/`phase_parent` continue to pass; new tests cover the timeout-reconciliation paths (unit tests in the implement-skill test suite).
6. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Keep the session-per-child isolation and per-child worktree semantics unchanged (SA-0MTLCCIPU0050Q52, SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9).
- The reconciliation must be read-only against `wl` (no mutation of a possibly-terminal child's state beyond the existing finalise path); do not re-spawn a session for an already-terminal child (existing "terminal children are never re-implemented" guard).
- Do not change the actual per-child timeout mechanism itself unless the RCA shows it is wrong (the defect is the *consequence handling*, not the timeout).

## Existing state

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`:
  - `_default_session_spawner` (line ~5540) — timeout → `success: false`, generic reason.
  - `phase_drive` (line ~5620) — breaks on `not spawn_result["success"]`, no terminal-state reconciliation.
  - `_is_terminal_child` / `_is_terminal_status` (line ~765–804) — already used by `phase_parent`.

## Desired change

Modify `phase_drive` to perform a terminal-state reconciliation after a spawned child session times out (or exits non-zero):

1. After a `TimeoutExpired` (or non-zero exit) in the drive loop, call `wl show <child_id>` to fetch the child's current state.
2. Classify via `_is_terminal_child`:
   - **Terminal** (status `completed`/`done` or stage `in_review`): record the child as `ok` with `reason` noting "completed late — timed out after Xs but child is terminal". Do **not** break the chain; continue driving remaining children.
   - **Non-terminal**: preserve the existing hard-failure behaviour (break chain, report failed).
3. When all children are terminal (either originally or reconciled), advance the parent as usual.
4. For children that are non-terminal but have a commit pushed to `dev` (stranded in-progress): either finalise the status (if the existing finalise path supports it) or emit a clear diagnostic.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_drive`, `_default_session_spawner`, terminal-state helpers (`_is_terminal_child`, `_is_terminal_status`).
- `skill/implement/tests/` — extend drive-loop tests with a timeout-reconciliation fixture (injectable `spawn_session`).
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — terminal-state helpers; finalise path.

## Related work

- SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9 (completed) — implement skill: drive all epic children to completion (fresh session per child).
- SA-0MTLCCIPU0050Q52 (completed) — when implementing an epic, start a new session for each child.
- SA-0MUY9PYBD009Y7J5 (completed) — fix Pi turn_end boundary error in driven child sessions (child stderr noise; related child-session reliability).
- WL-0MVGEB3IP002V8IB (ContextHub epic) — the epic whose three driven children exhibited this in production.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption A1.** The observed real-world outcomes (false-negative failed report + stranded `in-progress`) are caused by the missing terminal-state reconciliation in `phase_drive` (the only code path consistent with "work pushed + item terminal, yet drive reports timeout failure"). This is the same defect class as the manual finalisation needed for WL-0MVGUA9EY003XFAD.
- **Assumption A2.** A reconciliation pass is preferable to raising the timeout: child sessions do complete; the timeout is a bound (not a verdict). Recommended fix: after a spawn timeout, re-fetch the child's state and classify.
- **Risk R1.** Fetching the child's state via `wl show` after a timeout adds latency to each failed spawn. Mitigation: only perform reconciliation on timeout/non-zero-exit paths, which are already the slow/failed path.
- **Risk R2.** The reconciliation might mask a genuinely stuck child (e.g., child committed incomplete work). Mitigation: only treat `completed`/`in_review` + pushed commit as terminal; if the child is `in_progress` with no commit, fail as before.
- **Risk R3.** Scope creep: finalising stranded in-progress items adds a mutation path. Mitigation: the mutation should be via the existing `StatusLifecycle` finalise path (read-only per the constraint); if no safe finalise path exists, emit a diagnostic instead of mutating.

# Fingerprint from item data only, v2 line

**Parent:** SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0 (Simplify audit freshness: invalidate only on this work item's own data change)

**User story:** As an audit operator, I want the audit content fingerprint computed from this work item's own data only, with zero git calls, so an unrelated commit — or even a change to a file this item touched — never invalidates a stored audit.

**Producer decision (2026-10-21, comment SA-C0MVIAGIQU003WW4P):** option (a) — the strict item-data-only formula (title + description, zero git calls) supersedes the per-touched-path formula from SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P. This is the core slice of the parent item.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_compute_content_fingerprint` hashes a canonical JSON payload of **exactly** `{"schema": 2, "title_hash": <sha256(title)>, "description_hash": <sha256(description)>}` (`sort_keys=True`, then sha256 hex of the serialised payload). No `path_states`, no `key_files`, no comment-derived input (the Key Files section is part of the description and therefore already covered by `description_hash`).
2. The computation performs **zero git invocations**: it does not call `_resolve_touched_files`, `_compute_path_fingerprints` or any `git` subprocess, and is correspondingly fast (no repo probing) — asserted by a test that patches the git-executing helpers to raise.
3. `_compute_content_fingerprint` returns `None` (fail open → full re-audit) only when the work item cannot be fetched (`wl show` failure) or the payload cannot be built; a missing/garbage description still yields a deterministic hash.
4. `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX` becomes the **versioned** `"Audit content fingerprint (v2): "`; `_extract_content_fingerprint` returns a value only for `v2` lines and returns `None` for unversioned legacy lines, so legacy reports fall through to the existing time-gate floor (`AUDIT_FRESHNESS_BUFFER_SECONDS` + persist-write tolerance) with **no silent mass re-audit wave**. All three persist sites (~5714, ~5740, ~6158) emit the versioned line.
5. The now-unused `comments` parameter of `_compute_content_fingerprint` is removed and every call site updated: `_check_audit_freshness` (~2020), `_get_child_audit_verdict` (~6606), `_run_remediation_loop` (~10171), `_phase_fetch_and_cq` (~10357), `_reaudit_budget_exceeded_children` (~10786), `_phase_children` (~11516, ~11918). `cmd_check_freshness` (~2117/2120) keeps working and reports `hasFingerprint` from the versioned line.
6. **TDD, same commit:** the per-touched-path and comment-contribution invalidation tests are rewritten to assert the new rule *before* the behaviour change, and the change lands only when `skill/audit/tests` is green — the repo gate forbids a red commit, so code + test migration are one commit (`<WIP-id>: <summary>` recorded on this item).
7. Docstrings on `_compute_content_fingerprint`, `_check_audit_freshness`, `_extract_content_fingerprint` and `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX` describe the item-data-only, zero-git, versioned-line contract; no docstring still claims path/worktree/comment components.
8. Verdict semantics unchanged: `--force` still bypasses the gate; the freshness skip still returns the stored `rawOutput` verbatim (an explicit `Ready to close: No` is never masked).

## Minimal implementation

- Rewrite `_compute_content_fingerprint` in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` to the item-data-only payload; drop the `comments` parameter and its plumbing.
- Version the prefix constant and make `_extract_content_fingerprint` version-aware (v2 only; legacy → `None`).
- Migrate the affected tests in `test_audit_runner_freshness.py`, `test_audit_runner_check_freshness.py`, `test_no_breakage_chore.py`, `test_audit_runner_remediation.py` (literal-prefix assertions → the v2 constant).
- Keep `_resolve_touched_files` untouched (still used by the Phase-2 file-scope manifest at ~5257/~7964/~10897); dead-code removal is a separate item.

## Constraints

- Read-only: no test-suite execution or `pi` calls from the fingerprint path.
- Do not re-design the consumers (child reuse, read-only probe, ship `isAuditFresh`) — they must keep working against the simplified formula, not be extended.
- Documented trade-off (accepted): a stored audit may reference code that later changed, including files this item touched. The audit verdict remains the record for the item's own data.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_compute_content_fingerprint`, `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX`, `_extract_content_fingerprint`, `_check_audit_freshness`, persist sites, call sites
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_freshness.py` — rule migration

- `skill/audit/tests/test_no_breakage_chore.py` — literal prefix assertions
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_remediation.py` — literal prefix assertion

# Parent Phase-1 screen: budget, batching and JSON robustness

**Parent:** SA-0MVF1NKZQ009P3ZG — Audits take too long: investigate and speed up
**Discovered-from:** SA-0MVI6VVC00029XO4 (post-change measurement, gate NOT met)

## Problem statement

The epic's post-change measurement (SA-0MVI6VVC00029XO4) ran a clean-room
single-item audit at commit `89aba34c5` and the AC6 gate was **not** met: 4
calls, 4,419.8 s (73.7 min) of LLM wall clock for ONE item against a ≤ 10 min
target. The measured cost was dominated by the **parent Phase-1 screen** — the
`+1` of the N+1 structure that no epic child owned:

| Context | calls | elapsed | note |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `false-positive-screen` | 1 | 247.4 s | |
| `parent` (Phase 1 parent screen) | 1 | **1800.0 s** | hit the 1800 s budget exactly |
| `verdict_reask` | 1 | **1147.4 s** | the parent screen's JSON was unparseable |
| `phase2_deep` | 1 | 541.1 s | |

Why it is unmitigated today:

1. The 1080 s right-sized budget applies to **child** screens only; the parent
   screen keeps the full 1800 s (SA-0MVI3608M0080QLW).
2. `--batch-phase1` folds **pending child** screens into one call; the parent
   screen is still a separate call (SA-0MVI6VRJT005M650).
3. `--phase1-model` defaults to unset, so the parent screen runs on the resolved
   model even when a faster Phase 1 model is available.
4. An unparseable parent screen triggers the most expensive call in the run
   (`verdict_reask`, 1147 s here).

A single-item audit has no child screens at all, so every child-path lever the
epic delivered is inert for it — the epic's primary user story ("single-item
audit ≤ 10 minutes") is gated on this call.

## Goal (user story)

As a release producer, I want the parent Phase-1 screen to be bounded and
robust like the child screens, so a single-item audit can meet the ≤ 10 minute
target instead of being dominated by one call at its cap plus a re-ask.

## Acceptance criteria

- The parent Phase-1 screen is folded into the same batched call as the child screens under `--batch-phase1` (one `phase1_batch` call covering parent ACs, indexed separately), OR it gets its own measured right-sized budget with the same derivation discipline as the child budget (`ceil(p95 x safety factor)`, documented, re-derivable).
- A test proves a single-item (no children) audit under batching issues ONE Phase 1 call, not two, with `met`/`unmet`/`partial`/`adjusted` semantics unchanged and the ready-to-close gate untouched.
- A capped parent screen is quarantined exactly like a capped child screen: evidence names the budget and phase, and the run increments a parent-screen counter in `AUDIT_RELIABILITY_SUMMARY`.
- A clean-room re-measurement of the same single-item audit (5 ACs, same command shape as SA-0MVI6VVC00029XO4) shows the single-item audit's total LLM wall clock within the ≤ 10 minute target on a healthy proxy, recorded in `docs/dev/audit-performance-baseline.md` with the before/after table.
- The parent epic's AC6 gate is then re-assessed on that evidence (≥ 50 % reduction vs the committed baseline, `partial`-fallback rate not increased, no closure-criterion relaxation).
- Full project test suite passes.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Phase 1 parent screen call site, `_phase1_review_children_batched`, budget resolution, reliability counters
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_phase1.py` — parent-screen batching/budget tests
- `docs/dev/audit-performance-baseline.md` — re-measurement section
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — parent-screen budget/batching behaviour

## Constraints

- Verdict semantics and the ready-to-close gate stay frozen (parent epic §Constraints).
- Do not raise timeouts to mask the cost; reduce or bound the work.
- Only 2 local proxy slots — stay below saturation.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk (quality):** folding parent ACs into the batch call could dilute parent verdicts — mitigated by indexing parent ACs separately and asserting parity on a fixed item set, as SA-0MVI6VRJT005M650 did for children.
- **Assumption:** the 1800 s parent cap is not a hard requirement; the ≤ 10 min user story requires the parent screen to complete far below it.
